evaluation.status: Predeclared version 1, frozen 2026-10-17 before any MESH grid value was decoded by this workstream. Any change needs a new version number and a stated reason.
evaluation.purpose: Measure how often MRMS MESH agreement with observed hail reports holds, by size class, in Montana, and state what that agreement can and cannot support. It is not a damage, roof or address measure, and it does not rank products.
questions: Report level: for each hail report at or above a size class, is there a MESH cell at or above that class within R km on the same SPC day (hit) or not (miss)?

Object level: for each connected MESH object at or above a class on a day, is there any report at or above that class within R km (object false alarm if not)? Reported as an upper bound because reports are incomplete.
Size: for hits, how far is the MESH maximum within R km from the reported size (median and mean absolute error, inches and mm)?
Stratified: do rates change by year, season, LSR qualifier (E, M, U), distance to the nearest Montana NEXRAD site, and night versus day?

reference_observations.primary: IEM LSR rows with TYPETEXT HAIL (VALID in UTC; MAG in inches; QUALIFIER E, M or U). Two strata: all rows, and M-only rows.
reference_observations.secondary_same_reports: SPC raw daily hail CSV (UTC; 1/100 inch). Hail of 1.00 in or more only (191 of 192 IEM rows match in 2025). Cannot serve the 0.75 in class. Not independent of LSR.
reference_observations.completeness_and_cross_check: Storm Events hail rows (local standard time, add 7 h for MST-7; verified for one June event, to be checked on a sample of DST and standard-time events before pooling). SWDI nx3hail (GMT) is a radar-algorithm cross-check only; it is not ground truth. Reviewer: in 41 of 73 July-August matches the SPC report time is 60 min later than begin plus 7 h; use a 60 min tolerance until resolved.

evaluation.time_window: SPC reporting day D: 12:00 UTC on day D to 11:59 UTC on day D+1. The MESH value is the MESH_Max_1440min file valid 12:00 UTC on day D+1 (listed about 8 minutes later; use the listing time, not the valid time, for availability). Window definition of the 1440 product is an open question (see open_questions). Reviewer: the 12:00 file equals the 720-step two-minute maximum (6,579 cells).

spatial_match.rule: A report matches a MESH cell when the cell centre is within R km (great-circle). The circle is a search area, not a footprint. Primary 15 km follows the W1 Benchland check; D17's 5 mile search radius (about 8 km) is reported as a sensitivity case. Reviewer: centre = report coordinates (a 12.7 km shift changes the Benchland 1.75 in outcome).

size_classes.why: 1.00 in is the severe threshold (25 mm); 1.75 in is the D17 tier 1 threshold; 0.75 in is the pre-2010 severe class; 1.50 and 2.00 in follow the brief.

event_definitions.report_hit: A report at or above a class, matched within R km on day D to a MESH cell at or above the same class.
event_definitions.report_miss: A report at or above a class with no MESH cell at or above that class within R km on day D.
event_definitions.object_false_alarm: A set of 8-connected cells at or above a class on day D with no report at or above that class within R km of any cell in the set. An upper bound.

metrics.POD_report: hits / (hits + misses) by class; Wilson 95% interval; day-block bootstrap interval for pooled rates.
metrics.FAR_object: object false alarms / objects, by class; labelled an upper bound.
metrics.size_error: For hits: MESH maximum within R km minus reported size, median and mean absolute error, in inches and mm.
metrics.conditional_reliability: Share of sampled grid points with a report at or above the class within R km, by MESH bin. Labelled a lower bound on the chance of hail, because reports are incomplete.
metrics.not_reported: Calibration and Brier score are not reported. They need a complete reference (hail pads, inspections or a dense survey), which Montana does not have in this data.
metrics.counts: Always report n, hits, misses, objects and days. No rate for a class with fewer than 30 reports in the held-out window; report counts only.

splits.development: SPC days 2020-10-14 to 2024-12-31 (after the MRMS version 12 upgrade). Used to check the pipeline only. No threshold is tuned on it in this version.
splits.held_out: SPC days 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31, excluding 2025-06-15 (the Benchland known example, roadmap item 11). Named days from the globe list: hail days 250613, 250614, 250620, 250721, 250728, 250807; quiet days 250603 and 250802 (raw SPC files confirm 0 Montana hail rows). Reviewer: SPC-filtered rule gives six named days; IEM rule gives twelve. Name one reference first.
splits.reserve: 2026-01-01 onward is not used by version 1.
splits.unit_of_analysis: The SPC day and the MESH object, not the pixel. Neighbouring cells are not independent.

strata: season (April to September versus October to March)
LSR qualifier E, M or U
distance from the report to the nearest of the four Montana NEXRAD sites (KBLX, KGGW, KTFX, KMSX; DECISIONS D24)
days flagged for a reference gap (for example SWDI 2025-06-15)
pre_checks: MRMS packing (8 or 16 bit) and version recorded by year before pooling.
Days with a missing 1440 file are listed, not zero-filled.
MESH values -1 and -3 are counted and excluded from maxima (not read as zero or as no hail). Reflectivity -99 and -999 are not used in this evaluation.
Reviewer: MESH_Max_1440min is 16-bit in 2025-06-16 and 2026-10-16; the 2025-06-16 two-minute listing has 718 files (window complete).
evaluation.exclusions: A day with a documented gap in any reference (for example SWDI 2025-06-15 after 03:29:26 UTC in the Montana box) is listed with the reason and excluded from the counts for that reference. It is not counted as no hail.
sensitivity: Window: SPC day versus the same day with plus or minus 6 hours.
LSR all rows versus M-only rows.
Raw versus filtered SPC files (for the same-report comparison only).
Exclude social-media-sourced reports (23 of 123 filtered 2025 Montana rows).
evaluation.reporting: Each rate with n, days, a Wilson 95% interval and the excluded-day list. No accuracy percentage without n. No best, no ranking of products.
what_it_cannot_support: Hail at any address, parcel or roof.
Roof damage, damage probability or insurance eligibility.
That no report means no hail, or that no MESH value means no hail.
Size accuracy at a point: the grid is about 1.1 km, the MESH value is a 24-hour maximum, and many reports carry estimated sizes.
Anything outside Montana, outside the held-out days, or about other products (AGENTS rule 9).

principles: Every per-location statement names its evidence kind, source, record or cell, time (UTC, and local with zone), resolution and original unit.
Evidence kinds stay apart (radar estimate, point report, station observation, modeled wind, official alert, forecast, inspection).
A count of addresses is 'addresses inside the estimated footprint', never 'damaged roofs' or 'customers'.
No report is not 'no hail'; no radar estimate is not 'no hail'; missing input is 'Data unavailable', never an all-clear.
Reports in inches as recorded; MESH in inches with the mm base value in brackets (WDTD: AWIPS shows inches; base values are mm).
SPC and IEM times in UTC; Storm Events times in MST-7 labels, with a 60 min tolerance until resolved.

required_lines.not_all_clear: No report is not "no hail", and no radar estimate is not "no hail". Missing data is shown as Data unavailable, not as an all-clear.
required_lines.not_damage: This shows weather near this location. It does not show that a roof was damaged, and it is not an insurance determination.
required_lines.export_line: Weather exposure does not confirm roof damage. This is an internal summary, not certified weather evidence. (DECISIONS D17)

templates.radar_estimate: Radar estimate (NOAA MRMS MESH): up to {size_in} in ({size_mm} mm) (the largest cell within {radius_km} km of this location, a search area), {window_start_utc} to {window_end_utc} UTC (SPC day {day}). Estimated maximum hail size from radar, not a measurement at this address. Source: MRMS MESH_Max_1440min, 0.01 degree grid, file {file_name}.
templates.radar_no_value: No radar hail estimate here: the MESH cells within {radius_km} km carry code {code} (meaning not verified). This is not an all-clear.
templates.point_report: Reported hail: {size_in} in at {place}, {report_utc} UTC ({report_local}, {zone}), {distance_km} km away. Source: {source_name}; size recorded as {qualifier_label}. One report at one place, not a measurement at this address.
templates.station_observation: Measured wind gust: {gust} {unit} at {station_id} ({station_name}), {time_utc} UTC, {distance_km} km away. Station observation, not at this address.
templates.modeled_wind: Modeled gust: up to {gust} {unit} in the model grid cell nearest this location (about {resolution_km} km), valid {time_utc} UTC. Model analysis, not an observation.
templates.official_alert: Official NWS {phenomenon} {significance} for {area}, valid {start_local} to {end_local} ({zone}). Matched {match_basis}. Hail tag: {hail_tag}. Wind tag: {wind_tag}. Text from the National Weather Service; this site does not write alert text.
templates.forecast: Forecast ({source}, issued {issued_local}): {summary} for {valid_local}. Forecast, not observed weather.
templates.inspection: Inspection record ({inspection_date}, recorded by {role}): {result_as_recorded}. Kept separate from the weather evidence above.
templates.data_unavailable: Data unavailable: {feed_name} did not load for this location and time window ({reason}). This is not an all-clear.
templates.no_report: No hail report within {radius_km} km in {sources} for {window}. No report is not "no hail". Reports are scarce in rural areas.
templates.address_count: {count} saved properties are inside the estimated footprint for {event_name} ({class_label} hail or larger, radar estimate). This counts properties in an estimated area. It does not count damaged roofs.

qualifier_labels.E: estimated (provisional until the code is verified)
qualifier_labels.M: measured (provisional until the code is verified)

forbidden_terms: all clear, except inside the required not-an-all-clear line
wording.check: A string check of every rendered sentence against forbidden_terms and required_lines, plus a browser check of each page (AGENTS rule 8).

privacy.owner_names: Owner name and mailing-address fields are in the statewide parcel data (OwnerName, CareOfTaxpayer, OwnerAddress1 to 3, OwnerCity, OwnerState, OwnerZipCode). None of them may appear in any page, export, index or log that the site publishes.
privacy.public_records: Parcel and address data from state and county sources are public under their own terms. The MSL metadata quotes MCA 2-6-1017 on distribution lists; a list built from addresses for contact needs counsel review before use.
privacy.constitution: Montana Constitution Article II, Section 10 (quoted in terms): individual privacy 'shall not be infringed without the showing of a compelling state interest.' Counsel should read how this applies to a per-address public page.
address_level_questions: Show hail history for named private properties, or only results for the visitor's own search? (owner and counsel)
Would a list of addresses used for unsolicited contact need MCA 2-6-1017 permission? Not checked here; counsel.
Do 'Inspection candidates' labels next to a named owner or address create risk? Owner names are excluded either way.
Does the public site need a lookup limit or notice to reduce bulk scraping? Not decided.

limits: Single-year samples are small: Montana 2025 has 61 Storm Events hail events at 1.75 in or more; 2023 has 16. Class rates need pooling and wide intervals.
Reports cluster in populated places. An empty rural area is not a negative observation (Wendt and Jirak 2021: MESH may add information where population density is low).
LSR, SPC daily and Storm Events hail rows largely share the same reports. SPC daily has no hail below 1.00 in. The SPC annual file matches Storm Events counts, not times (+60 min).
SWDI hail signatures are a radar-algorithm output: agreement with MESH is algorithm against algorithm. SWDI has no Montana rows after 03:29:26 UTC on 2025-06-15; the Plains box stops at 03:32:15 UTC.
MESH base units (mm) rest on the WDTD page (NSSL tables unreachable). The window is verified for one file; codes -1, -3, -99 and -999 are unverified.
LSR qualifiers E, M and U are inferred from the data; no IEM or NWS definition was found.
Murillo and Homeyer (2019) was read from the article page with a browser agent; no fit coefficient is used because they are not in the text.
The refuter decoded two 1440-minute files and one day of two-minute MESH; no hit or miss rate is computed on held-out days.
The SPC annual files supply counts only; timing uses SPC daily UTC files and IEM VALID.
NCEI and SWDI reuse terms are not verified beyond the NOAA disclaimer; the NWS and IEM texts cover their own pages.
Only the 12:00 MESH_Max_1440min files of two days were checked for listing time; the 2025-06-15 folder lags by a median of 24 minutes.
open_questions: What do the MRMS codes -1 and -3 (MESH) and -99 and -999 (reflectivity) mean? Needed before the evaluation separates no echo from no coverage. NSSL table unreachable here.
Answered for the 2025-06-16 12:00 file: equals the 24-hour two-minute maximum (fact added); the GRIB2 record has no window field.
What do the LSR qualifiers E, M and U mean in an IEM or NWS document, and which NWS rule sets how hail sizes are estimated or measured?
Answered: the filtered file applies SPC FAQ 6.11; raw keeps duplicates. Name one before the protocol is frozen.
Why does SWDI have no Montana hail signatures from 03:30 to 24:00 UTC on 2025-06-15? Test other dates and radars before SWDI is used as a reference.
Partly: the article reports no significant skill difference for MESH75 and MESH95 apart from peak-skill thresholds (29 mm to 40 and 64 mm); coefficients not in the text.
What are the NCEI Storm Events and SWDI reuse terms? The NCEI access page is a shell in this pass.
Open: June matches MST-7 exactly; July to August does not (60 min in about half).
Counsel (owner's decision): whether per-address hail history for named private properties should be published, and what contact rules apply to homeowners found through it. Not decided here.
Partly: MCA 2-6-1017 subsections (1) to (3) read; later subsections not read in full.
Calibration needs a complete reference (for example hail pads or inspection outcomes). Which source, if any, could provide one for Montana?
Should the held-out window grow beyond 2025 once 2026 SPC, LSR and MESH records are complete?

review.scope: Refuter pass: about 90 MB downloaded (cap 300 MB) in about 30 minutes: fresh copies of the SPC, IEM, Storm Events, SWDI, NCEI, NWS, NOAA, MSL, MCA and MRMS bucket files; MESH files decoded or tested; SPC FAQ, MCA and AMS article read; python -I, scripts outside downloads.
refuted_claims: SPC annual 'matches Storm Events exactly': counts match; times +60 min on all 190 rows.
Murillo and Homeyer 'not read': the article loads with a browser agent.
Installed licences: numpy, pygrib, pyproj, h5py carry licence expressions.
MESH_Max_1440min window 'not verified': the 12:00 file equals the 24-hour two-minute maximum.
SPC filter rule 'not stated': FAQ 6.11 states it.
Storm Events MST-7 in all months: June only; July-August 60 min off in 41 of 73.
SWDI gap as Montana-only: the Plains box also stops at 03:32 UTC on 2025-06-15.
SPC raw as complete 'same reports': SPC daily hail has no hail below 1.00 in.
corrections: SPC day page title: 'Storm Prediction Center 20250615's Storm Reports'; the UTC window is the heading.
Benchland: three SPC raw rows, three IEM rows and three Storm Events events.
IEM VALID is UTC: 165 of 166 unique matches exact, April to September 2025.
MCA 2-6-1017 restricts public agencies; subsection (3) covers individuals; company status is for counsel.
MSL metadata has no use-constraints or licence element; radar sites are in the predeclaration (line 81), not D24.
Match centre = report coordinates (15 km maximum: 51.3 mm at the SPC point; 35.7 mm at the W1 point).
Repo D13 dedupe differs from SPC's filter; radar_no_value should read 'code -1 or -3 (meaning not verified)'.
Decision time: the handoff keeps what was available at decision time; SPC files are preliminary, so record each download time.

Storm Events 2025 counts (190 hail; 61 at 1.75+; 309 thunderstorm wind); SWDI counts; usage text.

SWDI MAXSIZE units; LSR qualifier E, M and U definitions.
